title: Daily Market Digest: September 29, 2026
subtitle: Market closes mixed as investors eye economic data and geopolitical tensions

sections.title: Market Pulse: Wall Street Futures Edge Higher Amid Economic Cues

items.headline: US Futures Indicate Cautious Rebound Following Monday's Losses
items.summary: U.S. stock futures edged higher early Tuesday, with Dow Jones futures up 0.29%, S&P 500 futures gaining 0.25%, and Nasdaq futures leading with a 0.43% rise, as markets attempt to recover from higher Treasury yields and inflation concerns that dampened sentiment on Monday. Oil prices are retreating and Treasury yields are easing, offering some relief to investors.

sections.title: Major Indices Performance (as of most recent close)

items.headline: Dow Jones Industrial Average
items.statContext: Fell 0.67% on Monday due to rising crude oil prices and surging Treasury yields.

items.headline: NASDAQ Composite
items.statContext: Slid 0.9% on Monday, impacted by weak performance from technology companies.

items.headline: Pershing Square Jumps on Fund Interest
items.summary: Pershing Square ($PS) rallied 5.36% driven by strong investor interest in its fund structure and portfolio positioning.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks Surges on Price Target Hike
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks ($PANW) climbed 4.63% after BTIG raised its price target for the cybersecurity firm to $425, accompanied by supportive commentary.

items.headline: MongoDB Plummets After CEO Resignation
items.summary: MongoDB ($MDB) shares dropped 18.46% following the abrupt resignation of its CEO and a leadership change, ahead of the company's investor day.

items.headline: Industrials Lead While Communication Services and Energy Lag on Monday's Close
items.summary: On Monday, the Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) saw a 1% increase, while the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR (XLC) and the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) both experienced declines of 0.9%. This indicates a rotation as investors assess inflation and geopolitical risks.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Signals: Flat Durable Goods, Steady Small Business Employment, and Shaky Consumer Sentiment
items.summary: August durable goods orders remained flat at $338.6 billion, though core business spending (nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft) rose 1.6%. The University of Michigan consumer sentiment index sits at 48.1, with short-term inflation expectations near 5%, indicating household pressures. Meanwhile, the U.S. small business employment rate held steady in September, with a slight increase of 0.02 percentage points in job growth and hourly earnings growth remaining below three percent (2.78%).

items.headline: Fed Rate Hike Probability Rises for October Meeting
items.summary: The CME FedWatch tool now shows a significant 70.3% probability that the Federal Reserve will raise the Fed funds rate by 25 basis points in its October FOMC meeting, targeting a range of 4-4.25%. This marks an increase from 57.6% a week ago, reflecting persistent inflationary concerns.

items.headline: CarMax, Carnival, and Others Report Earnings Today
items.summary: Several major companies are scheduled to report earnings today. Among them are CarMax ($KMX), Carnival ($CCL), Uranium Energy ($UEC), and Concentrix ($CNXC). Investors will be watching these reports for insights into corporate performance and future guidance.

items.headline: Oil Prices Stabilize as US-Iran Talks Continue
items.summary: Global shares are mixed, and oil prices have stabilized on Tuesday amidst uncertainties surrounding U.S.-Iran talks and the potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Renewed diplomatic efforts have led to a retreat in crude prices.
